name: The practitioner answer to 'which inference engine is best' is a situation table, not a winner; asking for a ranking is answered by refusing the framing
symptom: A buyer or engineer asks which inference engine is best. The high-scoring replies do not name one. The most-cited framing is that the question is malformed: 'It's often very silly to ask "which is better?" between tools. Which is better: a screwdriver or a hammer?' (15 upvotes). The most complete answer maps engines to situations and opens by saying 'It depends heavily on your situation.' The practical failure mode this record guards against is that a general-reader summary of 'the community prefers X' is simply false: in this corpus no single engine is preferred, and the preference is a function of user count, hardware vendor, quantization format, and whether the box is a laptop or a datacenter.
root_cause: The community has converged on a stable decision boundary that is cheaper to communicate than a ranking. Consensus boundary: llama.cpp for single user, consumer/edge, GGUF, CPU offload, mixed CPU+GPU, and AMD; vLLM or SGLang past roughly four concurrent users or any multi-GPU tensor parallel; TensorRT-LLM when you own the hardware and can absorb a build step. Two of the top answers in separate threads independently refuse the ranking framing, so this is not one contrarian.
workaround: State the situation before naming an engine, and treat any 'X is the best engine' claim without a user-count and hardware qualifier as unsourced. See sent-llamacpp-single-user-consensus, sent-vllm-enterprise-default-consensus, sent-sglang-multinode-and-prefix-consensus for the individual cells.
notes: This is the governing record for the whole sentiment layer. Vote counts cited throughout these records are a popularity proxy observed at access time, never a measurement - see sent-vote-counts-are-a-popularity-proxy-not-a-measurement. Reader-facing consequence: 'what should I use' has no answer in this repo's corpus; only 'what should I use for a single user on a 3090 with a 70B GGUF' does.
